reconcile.note: Gill reads the single 'day' of Genesis 2:4 as shorthand for the whole six-day span rather than one literal day, so it sets no rival one-day timeline against Genesis 1.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Julius Wellhausen treats the single 'day' formula in Genesis 2:4 as a signature of the older J narrative, never composed to fit the six-day P scheme that opens Genesis 1.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (Eng. trans. 1885; German 1883).

sides.snippet: God called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night. There was evening and there was morning, one day.
sides.verseText: God called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night. There was evening and there was morning, one day.

sides.snippet: This is the history of the generations of the heavens and of the earth when they were created, in the day that Yahweh God made earth and the heavens.
sides.verseText: This is the history of the generations of the heavens and of the earth when they were created, in the day that Yahweh God made earth and the heavens.
